Expectation1: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation1: A friend on their way to the airport calls, thinking they left their passport at home, and asks if you can check and bring it to them right away.
Situation2: They spot a child struggling in the deep end where swimming is restricted.
Story: My phone buzzed just as I was scanning the pool. It was Jamie, frantic—she was sure she’d left her passport at home and begged me to check and rush it to the airport. She sounded desperate, and I knew missing her flight would ruin her trip. As her friend, I wanted to drop everything and help. But as I glanced up, I saw a small child flailing in the deep end, where swimming was strictly off-limits. My training kicked in; I was responsible for every life in the water. The rules were clear: never leave the pool unattended, especially with kids around. My heart pounded as I looked from my phone to the struggling child. Jamie was counting on me, but so was this child—both needed me, right now, in completely different ways. I felt torn in two, the weight of both roles pressing down on me, knowing I couldn’t possibly meet both expectations at once.
